id: D15-0 gate: networks with the label error of termination frames weighted up
author: first_agent (group manager)
entrant: 2026-10-05 21:0xZ: 'Priprav tie nove materialy teraz' (after I named this as the one untried direction from the shot anatomy)
why: D13: the scalar heads' squared error is concentrated in the termination and low-current frames (tail regime: 18 % of frames; 70 % of the li error, 67 % q95, 41 % betaN, 52 % z_axis, 44 % volume). The networks' loss gives every frame the same weight and the labels 0.05 against the flux coordinates, so that regime is a small part of what they are fitted to. D14: trees fitted on the tail alone are too weak. A network keeps the shared trunk and all the data and can still be told that the tail's label error counts more.
change: fit_on_accelerators unchanged except the row weights of the LABEL error (its existing shot_balance path): tail frames weigh 5 times the others, scaled to mean one (about 2.9 against 0.58). The flux coordinates' error is not reweighted. Tail regime as in D14: fewer than 25 frames to the record end, or feature 62 (Ip / discharge peak) < 0.6, or feature 64 (seconds since start) < 0.3.
networks: four S16 members per fold with their original settings and seeds: recipe indices 0 (c), 22 and 24 (h), 31 (hx); fitted on the training part only (no calibration rows, also for members that originally had them), no readout-bank refit. Folds and reserved stems as protocol_kfold_oof_maps_20260929. Kaggle 2xT4, jax[cuda12] 0.8.2.
failed_fit_rule: amendment 1 of the K-fold protocol applies in spirit: a member whose calibration flux R2 is below 0.999 is reported; the gate is evaluated with whatever four networks the kernel wrote, and a fold with a failed member is flagged in the result. No retry before the first evaluation.

measure.text: the four networks' mean heads on every held-out frame of their fold, blended into the S16 out-of-fold heads (nn_oof.npz) with nested weights; variant 'regime' uses separate weights inside and outside the tail. Same head-level proxy and shot bootstrap as D9-0. Reported too: one weight; the D9 tree blend; both together.

rule: PASS if dS_proxy(regime) >= +3e-5 with bootstrap P >= .95. PASS -> deployment protocol: tail-weighted members fitted on all data and blended into the 195-net heads with the out-of-fold regime weights, together with the D9 trees if 'both' exceeds 'trees' by more than 1e-5; public score as the meter. FAIL -> closed; one weight (5) only, no second value.
limits_known: The comparison is S16 against S16 plus four differently weighted networks, so part of any gain could be plain ensemble growth (16 -> 20); ledger 2.10 puts 16 -> 65 at about +1e-4 S in total, i.e. four more plain members are worth well under 1e-5, and the regime weights show whether the gain sits in the tail. The reweighting may cost the heads outside the tail; the 'rest' weight is free to go to zero.
exposure: D13, D14 and D9 results known. No tail-weighted network exists at freeze.
